topic: How would the 0.25 dB passband loss affect link budget margins in low-noise satellite receiver frontends?
consensus_response: The 0.25 dB passband loss reduces effective received signal power, increasing noise floor and degrading SNR. This necessitates higher transmit power or lower noise temperature to compensate for the loss, impacting link margin. The increased power can introduce intermodulation distortion (IMD) and adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR), further degrading system performance. To mitigate these effects, design must balance trade-offs between complexity, interference issues, and potential thermal problems, often leading to increased system power consumption.
